=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary note on the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's note asserts that clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted" the disclosure framework and limitation package. That is not correct and is not binding on us — nothing in the baseline reflects any such agreement, and the note is simply the counterparty's attempt to narrow our review. I have reviewed every clause on its merits. We should also respond to the Seller in writing that no clause is agreed until the SPA is signed.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** Higher cap — ideally 50–100% of price for a company with identified concentration risk (Bluefen ~30% of revenue), open IP title (Ironquay), and an unresolved privacy incident; at minimum, cap applies only to general warranties with everything else carved out.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50% (AUD 12m) with specific indemnities, tax, title/capacity and fraud outside the cap. *Reason: 20% is the low end of the market and inadequate given the number of known, unquantified exposures in the DD record.*

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis (~AUD 10,000–15,000), basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%), and **tipping/first-dollar** recovery; related claims aggregated for de minimis purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Reject excess-only; propose de minimis AUD 12,500, basket AUD 240,000 tipping basket, with aggregation of related claims and no thresholds for specific indemnities/tax/fundamental. *Reason: An excess-only basket plus a high de minimis effectively gifts the Seller the first AUD 250,000 of every loss and lets the Sandbar-style AUD 110,000 items be split below thresholds.*

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months, and limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties (covers two audit cycles); tax 7 years (or statutory period + 6 months); fundamental warranties 6–7 years; specific indemnities until the underlying matter is resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Counter 24 months general / 7 years tax and fundamental; delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with an express schedule of what each limit covers. *Reason: 18 months may lapse before the first full post-Completion audit surfaces accounts issues, and the catch-all drafting sweeps indemnities into the short window.*

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency) capped at **100% of price**, time limit 6–7 years, outside de minimis/basket, and not qualified by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. *Reason: If title fails the Buyer loses the whole AUD 24m, so a AUD 4.8m cap on title warranties is commercially unacceptable and off-market.*

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Silent — no fraud carve-out appears; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 purport to apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a full fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out as a non-negotiable. *Reason: Attempting to limit liability for fraud is unenforceable in any event and its absence signals the Seller's drafting is overreaching across the whole package.*

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 "as at 22 Sept 2026"), the Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only of matters **fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no general disclosure of public registers; data room disclosure limited to a frozen, indexed USB/index annexed to the Disclosure Letter; specific indemnities unaffected by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure of public records entirely; accept data-room disclosure only on a "fairly disclosed" standard against a fixed index. *Reason: Disclosure of "publicly searchable records" would deem us to know everything on ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia and court registers, eviscerating the warranties.*

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. If any knowledge qualifier survives, confine it to **actual knowledge** of a short named list of deal-team individuals, of matters fairly disclosed, and expressly exclude constructive/imputed/adviser knowledge and "discoverable" matters.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3; fall back to actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals only. *Reason: "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge converts every warranty into a diligence exercise and makes the warranty package close to worthless.*

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 admits no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent as a **condition precedent to Completion**, in a form acceptable to the Buyer (acting reasonably), unconditional or with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; Seller to use **best endeavours**; a long-stop date; plus a warranty that no Bluefen termination/renegotiation has been threatened. Consider a price adjustment/escrow if consent is conditional.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a CP with Buyer approval of form, best endeavours and long-stop. *Reason: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of revenue and an unconditional change-of-control termination right is an existential risk to the valuation.*

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Consistent with debt-free/cash-free: payout at Completion from the purchase price via the funds flow, with **executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion** (or bank payout letter confirming release on receipt of funds); change-of-control consent under cl 8.1 or repayment as a CP.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require payout and release as Completion deliverables with price deduction. *Reason: Taking a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and only a promise of release is inconsistent with the agreed debt-free basis and leaves us exposed to a cl 8.1 default on day one.*

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 admits they're conditional on Completion and continued employment, and silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses (plus superannuation, payroll tax, and any employer on-costs — likely ~AUD 480,000+ all-in) treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt-like items** deducted from price or paid by the Seller at Completion through the funds flow, with a specific indemnity; confirmation of who the recipients are and whether any are flight-risk key staff.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise in funds flow as a price deduction grossed up for on-costs, with specific indemnity. *Reason: These are triggered by Completion and would otherwise be paid by the Company (i.e. by us) post-Completion, so "a matter for the Seller" is only true if the Seller actually funds them.*

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (cl 11.1), "considered adequate". DL §4 admits AUD 180,000 open, no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** Payment of the AUD 180,000 and delivery of a **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable (ideally CP); failing that, a specific indemnity covering not just the fee but all loss from any defect in title to the SOW3 Project Materials (re-development costs, licence fees, third-party claims, injunction risk), uncapped or capped at price, outside thresholds and time limits.
- **Recommendation:** Require payment + assignment at Completion; broaden indemnity to full title-defect loss. *Reason: Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 materials until payment clears — an indemnity for AUD 180,000 does nothing if the IP underlying the product isn't ours.*

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6 admits ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address, investigation incomplete, notification not assessed.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of the investigation (or at least a documented OAIC notifiable-data-breach assessment) before signing; a **specific indemnity** for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims, remediation), outside caps/thresholds/disclosure, with a 6-year tail; warranty that no other incidents exist; a Completion deliverable confirming deletion/recall of the file.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus pre-signing completion of the NDB assessment. *Reason: An unassessed export of 1,240 personal records is exactly the kind of known-unknown that general disclosure would otherwise bar us from claiming on.*

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL §8 says they must be read together and is silent on whether they're unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether these are pre-Completion liabilities (accrued → deducted as Debt-like/working capital), committed future spend (reflected in working capital target), or avoidable; confirmation they are not related-party or split to sit under the AUD 25,000/110,000 approval thresholds; treated as one matter for de minimis purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Request renewal documents and timing; treat any amount accrued or committed pre-Completion as a price adjustment, and aggregate the three for all threshold purposes. *Reason: Three identical AUD 110,000 contracts that the Seller says must be "read together" look structured, and a AUD 330,000 commitment is material against a AUD 250,000 basket.*

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 and cl 12.3 apply all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature"; fundamental warranties folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Clear separate regimes: (i) general warranties — cap/basket/18–24 months; (ii) fundamental warranties — 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (iii) tax — price cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) — price cap or uncapped, no thresholds, no disclosure qualification, no knowledge qualifier; (v) fraud — unlimited. Covenants and Completion obligations outside the limitation regime entirely.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft Clause 12 with an express limitation matrix by claim category. *Reason: The Seller's "one regime for everything" collapses the indemnities we are negotiating into a AUD 4.8m/18-month box, which defeats their purpose.*

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL §10 notes this is only the source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller's shares, review of constitution/shareholder agreement for pre-emptive rights, confirmation of no options/convertibles, and the **Riverlark security** position over the shares. Unqualified, uncapped title warranty and a Completion deliverable of executed transfer, share certificate (or lost-certificate indemnity) and updated register.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now; do not rely on the register, and reinstate full fundamental title warranty per SPA-N-004. *Reason: A company-maintained register is not conclusive, and with a secured lender in the picture we need to know whether Harbourglass's shares are charged.*

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:** A **tax indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or capped at price, 7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure qualification) and full tax warranties; IP warranties covering ownership of all Company IP, no infringement, and all contractor/employee IP assigned — with the Ironquay matter carved out into its specific indemnity. Both outside the general cap and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as open; insist on tax indemnity and IP warranties on the fundamental/extended regime. *Reason: Nothing in the baseline settles these, and for an analytics business IP ownership and historical tax are the two areas where a 20%/18-month regime is least appropriate.*

---

## Summary of priority asks for the mark-up
1. **Deal-structure items (must fix before signing):** Riverlark payout and release at Completion; Bluefen consent as a CP; Ironquay payment + assignment at Completion; bonuses deducted from price; independent title searches.
2. **Limitation architecture:** Separate regimes (general / fundamental / tax / specific indemnity / fraud); 50% general cap; 24 months general; tipping basket; fraud carve-out.
3. **Disclosure/knowledge:** Delete general disclosure of public records and the "discoverable" knowledge qualifier; "fairly disclosed" standard only.
4. **Specific indemnities:** DD-006 privacy incident, Ironquay, Riverlark, bonuses, tax — all outside caps, thresholds and disclosure.
5. **Process:** Reject the "pre-categorised [STANDARD]" framing in writing; nothing is agreed until the full SPA is agreed.

- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus pre-signing completion of the NDB assessment. *Reason: An unassessed export of 1,240 personal records is exactly the kind of known-unknown that general disclosure would otherwise bar us from claiming on.*

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL §8 says they must be read together and is silent on whether they're unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether these are pre-Completion liabilities (accrued → deducted as Debt-like/working capital), committed future spend (reflected in working capital target), or avoidable; confirmation they are not related-party or split to sit under the AUD 25,000/110,000 approval thresholds; treated as one matter for de minimis purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Request renewal documents and timing; treat any amount accrued or committed pre-Completion as a price adjustment, and aggregate the three for all threshold purposes. *Reason: Three identical AUD 110,000 contracts that the Seller says must be "read together" look structured, and a AUD 330,000 commitment is material against a AUD 250,000 basket.*

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 and cl 12.3 apply all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature"; fundamental warranties folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Clear separate regimes: (i) general warranties — cap/basket/18–24 months; (ii) fundamental warranties — 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (iii) tax — price cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) — price cap or uncapped, no thresholds, no disclosure qualification, no knowledge qualifier; (v) fraud — unlimited. Covenants and Completion obligations outside the limitation regime entirely.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft Clause 12 with an express limitation matrix by claim category. *Reason: The Seller's "one regime for everything" collapses the indemnities we are negotiating into a AUD 4.8m/18-month box, which defeats their purpose.*

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL §10 notes this is only the source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller's shares, review of constitution/shareholder agreement for pre-emptive rights, confirmation of no options/convertibles, and the **Riverlark security** position over the shares. Unqualified, uncapped title warranty and a Completion deliverable of executed transfer, share certificate (or lost-certificate indemnity) and updated register.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now; do not rely on the register, and reinstate full fundamental title warranty per SPA-N-004. *Reason: A company-maintained register is not conclusive, and with a secured lender in the picture we need to know whether Harbourglass's shares are charged.*

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:** A **tax indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or capped at price, 7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure qualification) and full tax warranties; IP warranties covering ownership of all Company IP, no infringement, and all contractor/employee IP assigned — with the Ironquay matter carved out into its specific indemnity. Both outside the general cap and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as open; insist on tax indemnity and IP warranties on the fundamental/extended regime. *Reason: Nothing in the baseline settles these, and for an analytics business IP ownership and historical tax are the two areas where a 20%/18-month regime is least appropriate.*
